question: Why do so many video hosts look straight into the lens and speak as if to one person?
answer: Because it imitates being spoken to. Horton and Wohl noted in 1956 that television hosts who address the camera create the illusion of a face-to-face conversation, and viewers answer with a feeling of intimacy. Vloggers chatting to the lens from their bedrooms have refined the same trick into a nightly visit.
move: Feeling spoken to is not the same as being known.
ask: Which voice on my screen feels like a friend, and what does it ask of me in return?
reference: Donald Horton and R. Richard Wohl, Mass Communication and Para-Social Interaction, Psychiatry, 1956
